To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the circulating plasma esterases, in particular the nonspecific, organophosphate-resistant esterases of high molecular weight, play a key role in the host defense against endotoxin.

the circulating plasma of endotoxin recipients is a major site of detoxification; that plasma esterolytic activity is a major determinant in endotoxin detoxification; and that the endotoxin-induced esterolytic increase in the circulating plasma is mediated through the heat-stable esterases of a nonspecific, carboxylic type.

the plasma esterase level increases in the rabbit following endotoxin administration and that the increased plasma esterase activity is associated with the increased ability of plasma to neutralize endotoxins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of mechanisms of host defense against bacterial endotoxin.
the mechanism of defense against bacterial endotoxemia in normal animals.
the mechanisms of host defense against the endotoxins of gram-negative bacteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the plasma esterase response in the normal animal represents a major host defense against the toxic effects of circulating bacterial endotoxins.
the normal animal is capable of mounting a defense against bacterial endotoxemia.
the normal rabbit is endowed with an effective and efficient system of defense against endotoxic shock.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the plasma of normal animals contains an endotoxin-detoxicating system that is activated by the presence of endotoxin and which is characterized in part by a heat-stable, esterolytic activity.
the normal host has a well-defined defense against the toxic effects of bacterial endotoxins and that this defense is mediated by the circulating plasma.
the normal host has a well-organized defense system for the prevention of endotoxemia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the plasma of normal rabbits contains a potent endotoxin-detoxicating factor.
the circulating plasma represents a primary site of detoxification of circulating endotoxemia and that the heat-stable esterases of plasma are of major concern.
the circulating plasma of normal animals contains an endotoxin-detoxicating factor which is not present in the plasma of animals which have been immunized against endotoxin.
